question: Children born blind, given sight by surgery at 8 to 17, could identify a shape by touch. Could they then recognise it by sight?
answer: Only after some days. Held and colleagues tested five such children in India soon after surgery: matching shapes touch-to-touch was near perfect and sight-to-sight good, but touch-to-sight was barely better than a coin toss. Within days the matching improved. Molyneux had put this question to Locke in 1693; it took three centuries to test.
move: Knowing a thing one way does not mean knowing it every way.
trap: A shape is a shape, whichever sense first learned it.
reference: Held et al., The newly sighted fail to match seen with felt, Nature Neuroscience, 2011
